abstract: We replace the supplied small GPT's GELU feed-forward sublayer with a near-parameter-matched SwiGLU network. Across two paired random seeds, mean full-validation BPB decreases from 2.07516 to 2.01698, a 2.80% relative reduction, at an identical budget of 9,830,400 training targets per run. Parameters increase by only 0.44%. The checkpoint selected exclusively on validation achieves 2.04783200 full-test FP32 CPU BPB, compared with 2.10270222 for the supplied baseline trained at seed 17 (2.61% lower). Results support a useful small-model improvement in this setting, rather than a general claim across tasks or training scales.
extension_method: A longer 4,800-step experiment was launched after the paired runs but produced no metrics or checkpoint before a reported system interruption. It contributes no result to the comparison. Further GPU training was stopped, and the final model remains a 1,200-step checkpoint; the interrupted attempt is disclosed in the run ledger.
validation_discussion: At seed 17, BPB decreases by 0.05554; at seed 29, it decreases by 0.06082. The consistent direction across the two paired seeds supports the mechanism, although two seeds are insufficient for a strong statistical-significance claim.

The gate-disabled branch is exactly the baseline, so the paired results also constitute a mechanism ablation. Only the FFN changes; attention, token budget, sampled windows, optimizer and learning-rate recipe remain fixed. The small parameter-count mismatch and differing FFN initialization are residual confounders.

Every completed run's best observed validation checkpoint is the final update 1,200. The best of the four candidates is gated seed 29. It was chosen before any test scoring; seed selection is disclosed and is not the claimed algorithmic contribution.
freeze_description: The frozen submission is the gated model at seed 29, update 1,200. It was selected using the lowest full-validation BPB among the four completed paired runs. The unmodified baseline seed-17 checkpoint is the reference. Both were scored repeatedly only after the candidate was frozen; no test-dependent tuning followed.
cost_description: The four completed full runs processed 39,321,600 targets in 83.69 measured training seconds and 155.16 trainer-process seconds (including preparation/validation). A separate 10-step CPU installation smoke test processed 81,920 targets in 5.98 training seconds (60.70 process seconds). The interrupted extension has unmeasured overhead and no saved results. Dependency installation/download and report generation are excluded; no pretrained checkpoint or earlier model ancestry was used.
limitations: The evidence is limited to WikiText-2, this tokenizer, a roughly one-million-parameter model, two seeds and a 1,200-update schedule. The curves still improve near the end, so this is not a claim of optimal training duration or best possible leaderboard score. Longer-budget results are unavailable.

Test improvement compares the validation-selected seed-29 candidate with baseline seed 17. It is not itself a paired same-seed architecture estimate; the two paired validation comparisons supply that evidence. Validation-based checkpoint/seed selection can still introduce selection bias.

CPU timing depends on background applications, process priority and hardware. Three trials summarize local runtime variation; they do not guarantee the exact instructor runtime. Peak memory uses conservative process-tree working sets, not GPU VRAM. Repeated test scores check determinism rather than estimating sampling uncertainty.
